chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it.

Behold, and indeed for everything is an essence, and the essence of the children of Adam is Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and us, and our Shites after us. How lovely are our Shites! How close they are to the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and how excellent is the making of Allah towards them on the Day of Resurrection.
By Allah! Had the people not magnified that, or pride entered into them, the Angels would have greeted them with kisses.

By Allah! There is no servant from our Shites who recites the Quran while standing in his prayer, except that for him there is a hundred good deeds for every letter, and if he recited while sitting in his prayers, except that for him there are fifty good deeds for every letter, and if not in prayer, except that for him there are ten good deeds for every letter.
And indeed for the silent one from our Shites is the reward of the one who recited the Quran from among those who opposed him.
You are, by Allah, sleeping on your beds, and for you is the reward of the Mujahideen; and you are, by Allah, in your prayers, and for you is the reward of those who stand in rows in His way.
You are, by Allah, the ones for whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And We removed whatever of rancour was in their breasts, [they are] brothers upon couches facing each other.'

Indeed, our Shites are the people of the four eyes: two eyes in the head and two eyes in the heart. Behold, and all creatures are like that, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, opened your eyes and blinded their eyes.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for reciting the Quran while sitting or silent according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the ontological essence (jawhar) of the Shia as rooted in Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing their elevated spiritual proximity to the Divine Throne. It quantifies the rewards for Quranic recitation across different postures and equates the merit of their devotional sleep and prayer to that of warriors in battle, a concept known as 'ajr al-mujahidin'. The narration concludes by interpreting the Quranic verse of 'brothers on couches' as a reference to the Shia, distinguishing them through 'four eyes'—two physical and two spiritual—highlighting their unique capacity for divine perception compared to others whose spiritual sight is veiled.
